It reports within-participant contrasts comparing conditioned drug cues (CSD+) and pleasant cues (CSP+) versus control CS− (CSD+>CS−, CSP+>CS−) and provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses reported; Tables S1–S2 and supplementary material) in addition to ROI/SVC analyses. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary references).

This is an empirical fMRI pharmaco-study in alcohol-dependent patients using visual alcohol cues. It includes within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral cues (task-evoked GLM contrasts at t1 and t2) and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume corrected (SVC, FWE) coordinates (e.g., VS, OFC, Amygdala, VTA). Coordinates and statistical thresholds are provided; MRI field strength (3T), participant demographics, cue type, and software (SPM12) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual high-calorie food images (natural reward cues). It includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food > nonfood control images, reports group-level voxelwise results within anatomically defined ROI masks (WFU Pickatlas) with voxelwise statistics and coordinates (i.e., small-volume/ROI-corrected voxelwise results), and also presents exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinate tables/figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This is an fMRI task study using standardized visual emotional (natural reward-related) stimuli (IAPS) with within-subject contrasts (positive>neutral and negative>neutral). Group-level voxelwise SPM8 analyses with whole-brain cluster-corrected results and coordinate tables are reported. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are described. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smokers viewing visual pleasant, unpleasant, neutral, and cigarette-related pictures (visual cue component). The analysis includes within-subject contrasts (cigarette-related, pleasant, unpleasant > neutral) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level GLM results with FDR correction and cluster thresholds; results are presented in tables and figures with coordinates for significant clusters. Preprocessing details and statistical software (BrainVoyager) and many MRI acquisition parameters are reported; MRI field strength (e.g., 3T) is not explicitly stated in the provided text (I7 is preferred, not mandatory). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette cue reactivity using visual presentation (participants held and viewed cigarettes vs neutral objects). The analysis includes within-subject contrasts of cigarette vs neutral cues (cue main effect and instruction×cue interaction) reported as voxelwise group-level results with tables/figures (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported; coordinates in Tables 2–3). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (NIS, AFNI). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it reports only seed-based task-modulated functional connectivity (gPPI) results (drug/alcohol cue minus neutral cue contrast in FC) rather than any group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual drug/alcohol cue reactivity using image blocks), I4 (within-participant contrast of cue vs neutral was computed), I7 (participant and methodological details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual alcohol-related and neutral pictures (visual cues) and reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are presented (multiple regression and one-sample t-tests), with correction for multiple comparisons (AlphaSim/FWE) and cluster thresholds; significant clusters (insula, caudate, striatum) are described and ROI-extracted activations reported. Necessary methodological details (participant age range, sex considerations, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing with SPM, statistical thresholds) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, is empirical with original human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using clear visual stimuli (personal and standard smoking vs nonsmoking pictures). The design includes within-participant contrasts of smoking>nonsmoking cues (personal smoking environments vs nonsmoking environments and standard/proximal cues). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results from exploratory whole-brain analyses (cluster-corrected threshold z=3.1, p<0.05) and ROI-based small-volume analyses, and presents coordinate/figure/table results. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cannabis cue reactivity that includes clear visual cues (pictures) within a multimodal paradigm and reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., cannabis picture > baseline; cannabis picture > flower picture). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-corrected; z≥2.3, p<.05) are reported, and a-priori small-volume (ROI) analyses (VTA, nucleus accumbens, pallidum) are also presented. Results are reported in the main text, figures, and tables; participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/AFNI/ANTS) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of tobacco cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related images and reports within-participant contrasts (smoking-related cues > neutral cues). Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted using mixed-effects FLAME with cluster-wise correction (Z>2.3, p=0.05) and results are presented in tables and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, 3.0T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT/FLAME) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-evoked human fMRI study using visual smoking cues (pictorial stimuli) with a within-participant contrast of smoking-related > neutral cues. Group-level voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and coordinate tables; thresholds reported p<0.001 and regression p<0.005 uncorrected), meeting the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked statistical results. Method details required/preferred (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength 3.0 T, preprocessing/statistical software SPM5) are provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity study of cannabis with visual cues, but the reported analyses are ROI-based dynamic functional connectivity (DCC) and topological measures rather than any group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts. The paper does not present whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results for drug-cue > control contrasts required by the meta-analysis. Therefore it fails the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result. Exclusion IDs E3 (only ROI/connectivity analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result) and E4 (connectivity-only analyses without qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (drug) cue-reactivity using visual video stimuli (first-person smoking vs neutral videos). The analyses include a within-subject Cigarette Cues > Neutral Cues contrast and report group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) with peak coordinates and tables/figures. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and stats software (FSL), participant demographics, and cue/task details. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines visual smoking cues and includes a within-participant smoking>neutral contrast, and reports participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing details. However, the full text reports extraction of beta-weights from anatomically-defined ROIs (left/right NAc and caudate) and subsequent regression analyses using those ROI values; it does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results (no coordinate tables, cluster SVC results, or whole-brain maps are reported). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses) while satisfying inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue fMRI), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), and I7 (reporting age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/software). It does not meet I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise result) nor I6 (no voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual monetary cues (e.g., ‘WIN $1’) to probe anticipatory reward/loss processing (natural reward-related cues). The MID task events were modelled and contrasted against implicit baseline (within-participant cue>baseline contrasts for anticipation phases), and group-level voxelwise whole-brain ANOVAs were reported (voxel-level p<0.001 with cluster FWE correction pFWE<0.05). A priori ROI small-volume-corrected results (insula, caudate) were also reported (SVC, pFWE<0.05). Necessary methodological details (3T scanner, SPM12 preprocessing/statistics, demographics, cue type) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (whole-brain and SVC voxelwise results), I6 (results clearly reported), and I7 (key reporting details present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study uses visual cigarette cues (appetitive smoking images) and includes within-participant Craving>Neutral contrasts at the single-subject and group (random-effects) levels. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with coordinates and cluster sizes (e.g., bilateral vmPFC BA10 clusters; Monte Carlo cluster correction described), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (BrainVoyager QX) and other methodological details are provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using explicit visual smoking and neutral cue pictures and a within-participant smoking>neutral cue contrast. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported: small-volume-corrected ROI analyses (SCC/PCC; SPM small-volume FWE-P values reported) and exploratory whole-brain cluster-level FWE results for cue-induced activations. The paper provides participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CONN), and includes sufficient methods, results, and discussion. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies with qualifying group-level voxelwise results.

This is an fMRI study using visual alcohol cues with a within-subject ALC>BEV contrast, but all imaging analyses are ROI-based: a priori 6-mm spherical ROIs were reverse-registered, average ROI timecourses extracted, and hierarchical linear models run on ROI averages (Bonferroni correction across five ROIs). The paper does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (neither whole-brain nor small-volume-corrected voxelwise maps or cluster coordinates) that would qualify under I5. Therefore it fails the requirement for voxelwise evidence and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (smoking and food videos) with within-participant contrasts (Smoking>Food, Smoking>Baseline, Food>Baseline). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain results are reported with cluster correction and tables/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T), cue type, preprocessing (FSL tools), and statistical software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-associated cues in abstinent alcohol-dependent patients and matched controls. Methods include a within-participant contrast of alcohol-associated versus control (neutral and scrambled) stimuli at the first level and subsequent group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. Group results were reported with small-volume correction (volume-of-interest correction) for striatum, ACC and mPFC and coordinates/tables are provided. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity and provides qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues vs neutral/control images with a within-participant contrast (alcohol > control). Group-level voxelwise analyses (whole-brain task effect with FWE correction) and small-volume-corrected ROI analyses in the ventral striatum are reported; results are presented as maps/tables and described in the text. Key participant details (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity that included a clear visual cue component (visual labels during taste delivery), used a within-subject alcohol>water (alcohol vs. control) contrast, and reported whole-brain voxelwise group-level results with cluster correction and coordinate tables. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type (white wine vs. water with visual labels), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs soft drink pictures). It includes within-subject contrasts of alcohol>soft drink (pretraining and pre-post), and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume FWE-corrected findings in anatomically defined regions (amygdala; reported coordinates and p-values). MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI cue-reactivity and provides qualifying voxelwise results.

This task-based ICA fMRI study meets I3 (visual cue-reactivity: drug, erotic, aversive, neutral pictures) and I4 (subject-level contrasts: drug>neutral beta-weights were computed), and I7 (reports participant sex/age info, cue types, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). However, it does not report any qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) for the drug>control or reward>control contrasts. The main inferential tests are performed on ICA component time-course beta-weights and ANOVAs (network-level), and the spatial maps are ICA-derived component maps rather than task-evoked voxelwise contrast maps with coordinates. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (only ICA/connectivity-focused analyses without a qualifying voxelwise task result) and fails inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete. Inclusion_criteria_applied: I3, I4, I7. Exclusion_criteria_applied: E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol pictures and matched neutral pictures, meeting the review objective. It includes a within-participant contrast (Alcohol>Neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise results including small-volume FWE-corrected ROI results in the striatum (ventral striatum and putamen) and whole-brain exploratory results with coordinates/figures. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and SPM8 software, and participant demographics. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (visual cues, within-subject cue>control contrast, qualifying voxelwise/small-volume-corrected results, coordinate/figure reporting, and essential methodological details). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual picture stimuli. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral control cues (alcohol vs. neutral picture contrast) and conducts group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (linear mixed-effects model in AFNI 3dLME) with cluster-wise multiple-comparisons correction (3dClustSim). Results are reported as voxelwise clusters/Z-scores and tabulated regions. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol pictures), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in cannabis-dependent humans using visual stimuli (33-ms images) including drug (cannabis) and natural reward (sexual) cues presented via a backward-masking paradigm. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (cannabis>neutral; sexual>neutral; aversive>neutral) at the group level. Voxelwise results are reported within an a priori ROI mask with small-volume (ROI) correction and cluster-level correction; peak coordinates and T-values are provided (Table 2) and figures display activation maps, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), cue types, and participant sex; core manuscript sections (intro, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue paradigm is individualized script-driven guided imagery (auditory/verbal) and does not include a clear visual cue component required by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts: drug-cue vs neutral were reported), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with family-wise error correction), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures/supplement), and I7 (participant age/sex and methodological details reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 do not apply). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the paper must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to visual cue-reactivity studies.

This full-text fMRI study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it used validated cigarette-related visual cue videos (visual stimuli) (I3); reported within-participant contrasts comparing cigarette cues vs neutral control (crave-allow and crave-resist vs neutral) (I4); performed and reported group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster correction (FLAME/FEAT, z-thresholds and cluster P-values) and tables/figures of coordinates (I5,I6); and it provides key methodological details including participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore I recommend inclusion.

The study uses an fMRI monetary incentive delay (MID) task with visual cues signaling reward, providing a natural reward-related visual cue component. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., anticipation of reward > anticipation of no outcome) and group-level voxelwise statistical results (voxelwise FWE-corrected activations and small-volume correction reported; coordinates provided). Participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting/ connectivity-only, and includes qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual reward cues (images of money, cigarette, neutral) and reports within-subject contrasts (money>neutral and puff>neutral) at the group level. The paper describes second-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (2x2 ANOVA) with significant reward type x abstinence interactions within a priori striatal ROIs; clusters are reported (voxel counts, coordinates shown in Fig.2), indicating qualifying voxelwise (small-volume/ROI) results. Participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is an fMRI investigation of smoking cue-reactivity using visual photographic cues, reporting within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > control cues) and group-level voxelwise results. Methods report whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with explicit thresholding (p≤0.001 uncorrected, cluster extent ≥20 voxels) and tables/figures of activations; scanner field strength (4.0 T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM5) and participant demographics are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets the review objective and required analysis/reporting criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (visual-only plus a small taste cue) comparing non–treatment-seeking alcoholic subjects and matched social drinkers. It reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > nonalcohol beverage cues and other cue>control contrasts, and performs group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM/MEDx) with cluster thresholds and reports activated clusters/tables (Table 2 and figures). The manuscript provides participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (MEDx, SPM99). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate drug/natural reward cue-reactivity using visual cues. It reports resting-state network coupling and a working-memory (N-back) task, not a cue-reactivity task with drug or reward visual stimuli, and thus lacks any within-participant drug-cue>control (or reward-cue>control) contrast required for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked WM results/ROI identification) and I7 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no drug/natural reward visual cue component), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I6 (no qualifying cue-evoked voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) strictly apply, so exclusion is based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for assessment.

The study uses the Monetary Incentive Delay task with explicit visual cues (reward, neutral, punishment symbols), fulfilling visual cue requirement. It reports within-participant reward>neutral contrasts (anticipation and outcome) and provides group-level voxelwise results: a small-volume-corrected NAcc activation for the reward anticipation contrast and whole-brain PPI connectivity results (cluster-level corrected). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images vs matched objects). It reports within-participant contrasts (food>object) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results analyzed with mixed-effects FLAME and permutation-based whole-brain cluster correction (i.e., whole-brain voxelwise results are available). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Therefore all inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI task-evoked voxelwise results are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-evoked, within-subject BOLD fMRI study in smokers using visual cues (cigarette, pleasant, unpleasant, neutral pictures). It reports a group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrast (cigarette > neutral) with tabulated cluster coordinates and figures (Table 2, figures), satisfying voxelwise whole-brain reporting. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager), and participant demographics (age/sex), and clearly include within-participant cue>control contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual alcohol cues (with a sip prime) and includes within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol vs beverage and alcohol vs control. Whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are reported (thresholded and cluster-corrected) with tables/figures of activated regions (e.g., nucleus accumbens, insula, cingulate). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM96, MEDx3.3) are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or lack of within-participant cue>control contrasts) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It uses a within-participant contrast of food pictures > low-level control pictures, reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results across the whole brain (FDR-corrected and uncorrected thresholds) with tables and figures of coordinates, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual cue-based reward reactivity and provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results suitable for meta-analysis.

This study used a Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task (monetary reward/punishment cues) rather than a drug-related or explicitly natural reward visual cue-reactivity paradigm. Although the paper reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction (I5) and presents voxelwise results in figures/tables (I6) and provides participant demographics and MRI details (I7), it does not provide a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4 not met). The visual stimuli here are task cues indicating monetary contingencies rather than evocative reward images typically used in cue-reactivity studies, so it does not satisfy the requirement for assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component (I3 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly triggered. Therefore the study should be excluded from this cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cannabis cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (full-color cannabis images) with within-subject contrasts of cannabis images > neutral/control images. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results, including small-volume-corrected ROI analyses (Z>2.3, cluster P<0.05 adjusted for small search volumes) and whole-brain cluster-corrected results, with activation clusters localized and reported (tables/figures). Participant demographics, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cocaine cues vs neutral cues, reporting within-participant contrasts (cocaine cues > neutral cues) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain results. The methods specify visual stimuli, GLM first-level contrasts (cocaine cues vs neutral), and higher-level mixed-effects whole-brain analyses with cluster thresholding; tables/figures and coordinates are described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported in figures/tables), and I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains the qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-subject contrasts (alcohol-cue vs neutral, stress vs neutral) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results with cluster-based FWE correction (p<0.001, cluster p<0.05; supplementary tables/figures). Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BioImageSuite, AFNI). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7).

The study is an fMRI task-based investigation of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes a within-participant contrast of smoking versus non-smoking control videos and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (t-maps, peaks in Tables S1–S2) with multiple-comparison correction (p<0.05 corrected). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (NIAK, fmristat), participant age/sex, and cue type are all reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-evoked BOLD fMRI responses to visually presented cues (backward-masked cocaine, sexual, aversive, and neutral images) in cocaine-dependent participants. It includes within-participant contrasts (cocaine vs neutral; sex vs neutral; aversive vs neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds (voxel p<0.005, cluster-corrected p<0.05), with peak coordinates and figures. Participant demographics, MRI parameters (3T), preprocessing (SPM8), and statistical methods are described. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It used visual alcohol-related pictures (I3). It reports within-participant task contrasts (alcohol-related pictures > neutral) used for ROI definition and group analyses (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported (voxelwise t-tests, corrected thresholds such as Bonferroni/FWE, T-scores, cluster sizes and Talairach coordinates) satisfying whole-brain/small-volume-corrected evidence (I5). Results and coordinates are presented in the main text/figures (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (TurboBrainVoyager, BrainVoyager, AFNI, FSL) are reported (I7). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Sample sizes are small (pilot), but that does not violate inclusion criteria.

This is a human fMRI study of heroin-related visual cue reactivity in methadone-maintained patients. It meets I3 (visual drug-cue paradigm), I4 (within-participant heroin-related > neutral stimulus contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results reported as activation maps and cluster results across the brain and within a priori ROI masks), I6 (voxelwise results presented in figures/tables referenced in the text), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, 3T field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (Alcohol Pictures Task) with within-subject contrasts of alcohol > non-alcohol beverage images. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain ANOVA results are reported (cluster-corrected to whole-brain α=.05 via Monte Carlo simulation) with coordinates and cluster statistics in Table 3 and Figure 2. Methods report participant ages/sex distribution, cue type (visual alcohol vs non-alcohol images), MRI field strength (Siemens 3T Allegra), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5 and AFNI). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using a multimodal taste paradigm that includes explicit visual labels (‘‘Alcohol Taste’’ vs ‘‘Control Taste’’), satisfying the requirement for visual cue content. It reports a within-participant Alcohol versus Water contrast (Alcohol>Water) and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain, cluster-corrected results (tables, figures, MNI coordinates). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/SPM procedures) are reported. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain analyses are present; not ROI-only or connectivity-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study of nicotine-dependent smokers uses visual smoking cues (images) and reports a within-subject contrast (smoke > neutral). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (cluster-thresholded Z>2.3, p=0.05) with tables/figures describing significant clusters, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise results. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), and participant demographics. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only without task-evoked results, between-group-only contrasts) are met.

The study is an fMRI task-based cue-reactivity investigation using visual cocaine and neutral images, reports within-subject cocaine>neutral contrasts, and presents group-level voxelwise results (SPM8; whole-brain cluster-level inference with reported coordinates). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant age range and sex composition, and cue type (visual cocaine images/paraphernalia) are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of drug-related (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual photographic cues. It includes within-participant contrasts (smoking cues > neutral cues) at the group level, with voxelwise random-effects analyses reported (tables of coordinates, figures) using whole-brain thresholding (p<0.005, cluster extent) and SPM5 preprocessing. MRI field strength (3.0 T), participant age/sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual beverage cues (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) presented in a block-design visual task, meeting the review objective. The study reports within-participant contrasts of each stimulus versus a mosaic baseline (i.e., cue>control contrasts). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed (second-level full-factorial ANOVA) with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and MNI coordinates reported. Voxelwise results are available in the main text/figures (regions, coordinates, F-values). Key methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue types, 1.5T MRI, preprocessing with SPM12/MATLAB). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical human fMRI study (pCASL on a 3T scanner) that used audiovisual smoking cues (multimodal design including a clear visual component) and a within-participant contrast of smoking cues > nonsmoking cues. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported, with small-volume correction (SVC) applied to a priori ROIs; peak coordinates and cluster statistics are provided in tables/figures. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, ASL toolbox) are reported. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical perfusion fMRI study of cigarette (drug) cue-reactivity using audiovisual stimuli that include clear visual cues. The study reports within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > nonsmoking/control stimuli and conducts group-level voxelwise analyses in SPM2 with cluster-level reporting and coordinates (p<0.001 uncorrected, extent threshold, tables/figures provided). Key details (participant age/sex/demographics, cue type, 3.0 T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-state-only; includes within-participant cue>control contrasts; is empirical). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual cues (cocaine words). It reports a within-participant contrast (cocaine > neutral words) at the group level using voxelwise random-effects one-sample t-tests and small-volume-corrected (SVC) inference within a priori ROIs. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant demographics, and cue type are reported. Although the authors report no significant clusters surviving p<0.05 FWE SVC, the required voxelwise group-level analyses and thresholds are described, satisfying the meta-analysis’ requirement for a qualifying analysis. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI cue-reactivity meta-analysis (visual drug cues, within-subject cue>control contrast, and reported voxelwise SVC group analyses). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines neural reactivity to visually presented natural reward cues (food images). It contains within-subject cue>control contrasts (Look Craved > Look Not Craved and Look Craved > Look Neutral). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (FWE-corrected clusters and coordinate tables), and a priori small-volume ROIs for nucleus accumbens are used. Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and SPM8 statistical software. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual natural-reward cue-reactivity and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol beverage pictures and emotional faces). It includes within-participant contrasts (alcpic > con, pospic > con, negpic > con) and reports group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain cluster correction (pcorrected < 0.05 using 3dClustSim) and tables of significant clusters/coordinates. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM8), and participant demographics are reported. Thus the paper provides qualifying task-evoked voxelwise (whole-brain-corrected) analyses of visual drug-related cues vs. control. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using validated smoking-related visual stimuli (ISIS) and neutral control images. It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > neutral (individual-level ‘Smoking > neutral’ contrasts) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (2-sample t-test and fixed-effect GLM contrasts) with cluster thresholds, MNI coordinates, and tables/figures. Scanner field strength (3T Philips) and analysis software (SPM8, MATLAB) are reported, along with participant age/sex and cue details. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-participant cue>control, or non-empirical) are met.

This study is a resting-state fMRI connectivity study comparing smokers and non-smokers; it does not include any drug- or natural-reward cue-reactivity task using visual stimuli nor any within-participant cue>control task contrasts. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without task-evoked results) and E5 (reports between-group contrasts without any within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports participant sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL)). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no visual cue-reactivity task), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is not eligible for this meta-analysis of task-based visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This fMRI study used a visual cue (conditioned stimulus) paired with a natural reward (juice) and reports within-participant, event-related contrasts (CS, UCS, PTDE, NTDE) with group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain and small-volume-corrected). The paper includes voxelwise statistical analyses reported in the main text and supplementary tables, reports participant characteristics (age range), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI). Thus it satisfies: I3 (visual natural-reward cue), I4 (within-participant event contrasts including cue vs baseline/other events), I5 (group-level voxelwise WB and SVC results), I6 (results reported in main text and supplement), and I7 (key methodological/participant details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual cues that predict cigarette (drug) and monetary (nondrug) reward, with trial-by-trial within-participant contrasts of reward-predicting cues (parametric increase in reward level, including a 0/no-reward level). Group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses (flexible factorial) are reported, with whole-brain thresholds and at least one FWE-corrected threshold; coordinates and cluster statistics are provided in the text (and supplementary). The methods explicitly describe visual cue presentation, 3T MRI acquisition, and use of SPM5 for preprocessing/statistics. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual stimuli (videos of cocaine and food) and reports within-participant contrasts (cocaine > food) with voxelwise, group-level statistical results corrected for multiple comparisons and reported as cluster/coordinate results (main text and supplemental tables/figures). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), AFNI preprocessing/statistics, and participant age/sex. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes a within-subject cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie; food > nonfood). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed using SPM12 and reported (factorial second-level whole-brain tests with cluster-level thresholds), and results are described in the main text and figures. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/software (SPM12), participant ages, and cue types are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling eligibility assessment. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for task-evoked visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies of natural rewards.

This is an empirical task-fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity that includes clear visual cues (unisensory visual pictures) and multimodal (visual+odor) conditions. It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral pictures (CIG-I vs NEU-I) under both odorless and cigarette-odor conditions. Whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses are reported (cluster-thresholded Z>2.3, p<0.05 corrected), and ROI post-hoc analyses are also presented. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study does not address cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards using visual cues. It employs a monetary reward (card-guessing) task examining anticipation and win outcome, not presentation of drug or natural reward visual cues. Therefore it lacks the required cue-reactivity design and does not include a within-participant cue>control contrast for drug or natural reward cues. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level voxelwise/small-volume-corrected ROI clusters were reported within ROIs), I6 (results referenced in figures/supplement), and I7 (participant age/sex and MRI methods reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (functional MRI assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component) and I4 (at least one analysis of cue>control stimuli for drug or natural reward cues). No exclusion criteria from the review’s list (E3–E6) directly apply beyond non-relevance to the review objective. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study is excluded for failing to meet key inclusion criteria I3 and I4.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual smoking cues and matched visual control cues (I3). It includes a within-subject contrast of smoking>control cues (I4) and reports group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses (one-sample and two-sample t tests) with coordinates/tables and figures (I5, I6). The authors used an a priori anatomical mask (WFU PickAtlas) to restrict voxelwise analyses to cue-related regions (i.e., a small-volume voxelwise approach) and report MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing, and SPM2 software as well as participant demographics (I7). Results are reported as voxelwise task-evoked activations (tables/figures) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Although the sample is small (n=15) and the mask-based thresholding used an uncorrected p-value, the paper nonetheless provides group-level voxelwise task results suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity studies.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation using visual food images (natural rewards). It includes a within-participant task-evoked contrast involving food cues versus baseline (described as “appetizing vs. plain > baseline”) at first level, reports group-level whole-brain corrected voxelwise results (FWE within-group, FDR between-groups) with cluster coordinates, and provides MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant age/sex, and cue type. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This study is excluded because it investigates nalmefene effects on emotional face processing (angry/fearful faces) rather than drug-related or natural reward-related cue-reactivity. While the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (faces > forms) with coordinate results and preprocessing/statistics (satisfying I5, I6, I7), it does not meet I3 (not an fMRI study of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual reward/drug cues) and does not meet I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control or natural reward-cue > control contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that investigates reward-related neural responses using a Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) paradigm with visual cues indicating reward magnitude (big vs small). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (anticipation of big vs small win) and submits these contrasts to group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (VBM-style and BOLD voxel-to-voxel t-tests) with appropriate thresholds and reporting of results (figures/tables/supplement). Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for (I3) fMRI with visual reward cues, (I4) within-participant cue>control contrast (big>small win), (I5) group-level voxelwise whole-brain results, (I6) results available in figures/supplement, and (I7) necessary meta-data reported. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cannabis cue-reactivity that includes visual (and tactile) cue presentations. It reports within-participant contrasts (cannabis>neutral, cannabis>fruit, fruit>neutral) and group-level voxelwise results using mixed-effects FLAME with cluster-level FWE correction (whole-brain voxelwise results reported). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, FSL/FEAT/FLAME), and cue types are described. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-evoked, voxelwise visual cue-reactivity are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the full text as provided does not report an explicit within-participant drug-cue>control (alcoholic images > neutral images) voxelwise contrast required for inclusion. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (study reports group treatment effects and fMRI activation differences but the provided text does not present or describe a within-participant cue>control contrast for drug cues). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used visual alcohol-related cues—pictures of alcoholic and neutral beverages). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no explicit within-participant drug-cue>control contrast for alcohol cues is reported in the provided text), I5 (no clear evidence in the provided text that a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result for an alcohol cue>control contrast is reported as whole-brain or small-volume-corrected), I6 (although the text references Fig. 4 and table S3, the provided excerpt does not include voxelwise coordinates or clearly accessible voxelwise results for the alcohol cue contrast). Because these key analytic details are not present in the supplied full text, the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual picture stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > beverage control cues (AUD group alcohol–beverage comparison) and group-level voxelwise results analyzed with SPM99, with cluster-level corrected P < 0.05 and Talairach coordinates reported (Table 3 and figures). MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99), participant descriptors (right-handed male and female college students, AUD vs controls), and cue types (alcoholic, non-alcoholic, control pictures) are reported. Full article text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study limitations). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of opioid-use disorder that used visual drug-related cues (drug, sexual, aversive, neutral) and reports within-subject contrasts (drug vs neutral) across sessions. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (whole-brain ANOVA with corrected cluster reported), and ROI small-volume analyses were also presented. The paper reports participant demographics, cue types, 3T MRI acquisition and SPM8 preprocessing/statistics. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary appendices are referenced but core content is present.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study that includes a clear visual cue component (45 s cigarette video cues) and computes within-participant contrasts (Cigarette Cues > Control Cues; Alcohol Cues > Control Cues). Group-level voxelwise GLMs were run (38 whole-brain GLMs) to define precuneus peak voxels (coordinates reported), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected task-evoked results; results are reported in text and with peak coordinates. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is original human fMRI data). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study of cigarette cue exposure with visual cue components and within-subject comparisons (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the paper reports ROI-based connectivity (uSEM/GIMME) and mean ROI activation ANOVAs rather than any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results or coordinate tables/figures are provided). Therefore it fails the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise group-level result (I5 not met). As a result, it meets exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only analyses without qualifying voxelwise results) and E4 (effective/connectivity analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on E3 and E4; inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7; inclusion criteria not met: I5 (and thus no qualifying voxelwise results as referenced in I6).

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual smoking stimuli and within-subject contrasts (cigarettes vs pencils/chairs), and reports participant demographics and MRI details. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with clear visual cue component) and I4 (within-participant cue vs control contrasts). However, the primary analyses are ROI-based MVPA in the lateral occipital complex; the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical contrasts (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) for drug cues>control stimuli (e.g., cigarette>pencil) suitable for coordinate-based voxelwise meta-analysis. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/MVPA results reported without qualifying voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Hence the study should be excluded from the voxelwise meta-analysis.

Full text appears complete. Met inclusion: I5 (authors report exploratory whole-brain analyses), I6 (results/supplementary material indicated for detailed voxelwise displays), and I7 (participant sex/age and MRI field strength reported). Not met / unclear: I3 (the manuscript does not explicitly state that the cue-reactivity task used visual-only cues or that visual cues were a clear component) and I4 (the paper does not explicitly present a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli voxelwise contrast in the main text — the description implies cue reactivity analyses but the necessary explicit within-subject cue>control contrast for task-evoked voxelwise results is not clearly documented in the provided text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met. Therefore, because key inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are not satisfied/are unclear from the provided full text, the study is excluded.

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. It reports first-level cue contrasts (highly desirable > less desirable food images) and group-level voxelwise paired t-test comparing walnut vs. placebo, with stereotactic coordinates and cluster-level FWE-corrected results (right insula: X,Y,Z 32,10,10; p<.003 FWE cluster), and provides MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8) and participant demographics. All required reporting for inclusion is present and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is original empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and reports within-subject contrasts of drug cue > neutral. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (voxelwise threshold z>=2.3, cluster-corrected at P<0.05) with reported peak coordinates and cluster assignments; percent BOLD signal change and predictive-value calculations are presented. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing software (FSL), and relevant subject demographics are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (visual cue component, within-participant drug>control contrast, qualifying group-level voxelwise results, coordinate reporting, and methodological details). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of smokers using visual smoking videos as cues, with a within-subject contrast of smoking>neutral videos. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain corrected p<0.05 and T-maps/coordinates), and provides participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and analysis software (fmristat). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a visual cue-based Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task (shapes signaling monetary gains/losses), constituting natural reward-related cue reactivity. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of reward-anticipation versus non-incentive (cue>control) and outcome contrasts. Group-level voxelwise statistical maps are presented and reported with familywise error correction (whole-brain voxelwise results and voxelwise t-tests), and VOI analyses supplement these results; figures and tables are referenced. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of cigarettes, money, neutral) in daily smokers. It includes within-participant contrasts (tobacco>neutral and money>neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses (voxelwise one-sample t-tests for disjunction mask with AlphaSim cluster correction, and a priori small spherical ROIs), with results described in the main text and supplementary materials. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), stimulus details, and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs neutral images). The paper reports a within-participant smoking>neutral contrast (first-level GLM) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (higher-level nonparametric permutation analysis using FSL Randomise) within an anatomically defined mask (insula, striatum, thalamus), with cluster coordinates reported (MNI). Key methodological details (participant sex/age counts, cue type, 3T scanner, preprocessing and software) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual picture cues (alcohol vs non-alcohol beverages). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > beverage) and group-level voxelwise statistical analyses using SPM5 (thresholds and cluster extent reported) with MNI coordinates and figures/tables of activation (including ventral striatum). Imaging was acquired at 3.0T and methods/results/discussion are present in the full text. Thus it meets the meta-analysis scope and all required inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural-reward (food) cues and includes within-participant contrasts of hedonic food cues > nonfood objects. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (SPM8 random-effects, cluster-corrected threshold with MNI coordinates and tables/figures). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using clear visual stimuli (videos in Study 1 and still images in Study 2). Both studies use within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > non-smoking control stimuli. Study 1 reports voxelwise group-level GLM results within an a priori ROI mask with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-size correction (i.e., small-volume/ROI-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results) and provides MNI coordinates; Study 2 provides ROI beta extractions and group comparisons and correlations. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM/FSL) are reported. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cannabis cue reactivity using visual cannabis vs neutral stimuli (blocked-design) with within-subject contrasts (cannabis > neutral). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (ANOVA and voxelwise t tests) are reported with cluster-level FWE correction and region-of-interest follow-ups; results are presented in the main text and supplementary materials. Participant demographics and cue type are described. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes visual stimuli (pictures) and olfactory cues. It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., HFHS>NF, HFHS>LFLS) and group-level voxelwise pre- to post-surgery T-tests using a whole-brain approach (p=.001 uncorrected, cluster threshold), with reported significant clusters and extracted beta values. MRI field strength (3T), participant demographics, cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, DARTEL) are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

The full text reports an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity task using visual stimuli and within-subject ALC>BEV contrasts, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), but imaging analyses are reported as ROI-based percent signal change from anatomically defined ventral striatum spheres rather than as group-level voxelwise (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) results or coordinate tables. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Only the abstract/full-text content provided; full text is incomplete so I cannot verify that a qualifying group-level voxelwise (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) task-evoked contrast is reported (I5). From the abstract, the study uses backward-masked visual cannabis cues and compares cannabis cues to neutral cues, satisfying I3 (visual cue component) and I4 (within-participant drug cue > control contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because the full article (methods/results) is not available to confirm voxelwise/statistical reporting and coordinate tables/figures (I5/I6), I must exclude this record pending full-text access.

The fMRI component used visual drug-word cues and included within-subject contrasts (drug>fixation and drug>neutral), satisfying I3 and I4. However, fMRI results are presented as ROI extractions and group-level ANOVAs rather than as group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results; no whole-brain or SVC voxelwise coordinates/clusters are reported in the text. Although whole-brain interaction testing is mentioned in methods, no qualifying voxelwise results are provided. Therefore the study meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result) and fails to meet I5. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual heroin-related cues with a within-participant heroin-related > neutral contrast, whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM8) with multiple-comparison cluster correction, and full reporting of methods, participants, MRI field strength, preprocessing and software. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cannabis cues and non-cannabis control images, with within-participant contrasts (cannabis>non-cannabis) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain cluster-corrected, z>3.1, p<0.05). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistics (FSL/FEAT), participant age/sex, and ROI analyses supplement whole-brain results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study is excluded because it reports ICA-based network component betas (DMN/ECN/SN) and temporal-sorting component-level associations with smoking and food cues rather than providing a group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrast (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) of drug>control or natural-reward>control. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (task uses ICA/time-course analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using clear visual stimuli: smoking and food video clips) and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not report a within-participant voxelwise drug>control or natural-reward>control contrast suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis) and I5 (does not present at least one group-level voxelwise or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical result). Full text appears complete. Therefore study cannot be included for a voxelwise coordinate-based meta-analysis of cue>control contrasts.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (images of alcoholic drinks vs water) presented during a Pavlovian-instrumental transfer task. The authors report within-subject voxelwise contrasts comparing alcoholic versus water stimuli (alcohol>water PIT), including ROI and exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analyses with a reported small-volume-corrected (SVC, pFWE−SVC=0.01) peak in the right ventral striatum (coordinates provided). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes qualifying task-evoked voxelwise SVC result; includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity but the experimental cues are gustatory (taste delivery of alcohol vs juice) rather than visual, so it does not meet I3 (visual cue component). It does include a within-participant contrast Alcohol>Juice (I4 met) and reports participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details (I7 met). However, voxelwise results are limited: primary findings are ROI-based, and the exploratory whole-brain analysis reported only uncorrected clusters (no whole-brain FWE/FDR-corrected or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results). Therefore it fails I5. Because the paper reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC-corrected result, exclusion criterion E3 applies. Inclusion met: I4, I7. Inclusion not met: I3, I5. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used olfactory (odor) cues during the imaging task (eyes closed, no pictures presented during scanning), so it does not include a visual cue component in the fMRI task and thus fails inclusion criterion I3. The study did include a within-participant AO>ApCO contrast (satisfying I4) and reports participant and methods details (I7). However, the primary statistical inferences were performed on ROI-averaged contrast values extracted with MarsBar and analyzed in SPSS; although SPM maps are displayed, the paper does not present a group-level voxelwise whole-brain or clearly small-volume-corrected statistical result for the AO>ApCO contrast (i.e., qualifying voxelwise inference is not provided), so it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise/WB or SVC result). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion IDs met: E3. Inclusion IDs met: I4, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: I3, I5. Detailed: no visual cues during fMRI imaging (I3 not met); no clearly reported corrected voxelwise or SVC group-level voxelwise result (I5 not met), so excluded.

Although this rt-fMRI study used visual natural reward cues (food images) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (up-regulation vs passive viewing; FWE-corrected), it does not report a within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food images or high-calorie food > neutral baseline) that would satisfy I4. The reported contrasts are primarily: (a) up-regulation vs passive viewing — both conditions present the same food cues and thus do not constitute cue>control, and (b) healthy vs unhealthy choice contrasts used for ROI selection but not presented as a qualifying group-level cue>control voxelwise result for the meta-analysis. Therefore I4 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study uses the Monetary Incentive Delay Task with explicit reward versus neutral cues (visual cue onset modeled), providing within-participant reward>neutral contrasts (MID reward-neutral). It reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain mixed ANOVAs, FWE-corrected voxelwise results and whole-brain activation maps) and ROI analyses. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore it meets I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant reward>neutral contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported in main text/figures), and I7 (participant characteristics and task/methods reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of stress-induced cocaine craving using personalized guided-imagery (audiotaped scripts) rather than visual drug or natural reward cues. Inclusion criteria I3 (clear visual cue component) is not met because the paradigm used auditory guided imagery, not visual cue presentations. Inclusion criterion I4 (a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward cues > control) is not met: the within-subject contrasts are stress (imagery) vs neutral imagery or imagery vs baseline, not a drug-cue (visual) > control contrast. The full text does contain task-evoked, voxelwise whole-brain results, so I5 is satisfied; results are presented in figures/tables (I6) and participant/method details reported (I7). However, failure to meet I3 and I4 means the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective, so it must be excluded.

This is an fMRI task-based study using visual drug cues (cocaine words) with a within-subject CW vs NW contrast. The authors performed group-level voxelwise SPM12 second-level analyses (one-sample t-test) for the CW minus NW contrast and report voxelwise cluster results (uncorrected clusters used and tabulated) and used these for ROI/DCM selection. Key methodological details are reported (participant demographics, cue type, 3T scanner, preprocessing and software). Although corrected whole-brain significance was not found, a group-level voxelwise task-evoked analysis is reported, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for task-evoked voxelwise results. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (appetitive food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.
