It includes a within-participant contrast of food>scrambled control stimuli, and reports group-level voxelwise results: whole-sample whole-brain one-sample t-test and group comparisons within an a-priori ROI with FDR correction (small-volume-corrected voxelwise results). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human smokers that includes visual cues (picture indicating puff, money, or neutral) during a rewarded-guessing task, satisfying the visual cue requirement. It reports within-participant contrasts of puff > neutral (drug cue > control) and money > neutral, with group-level voxelwise analyses conducted within a priori anatomical ROI mask (striatum and mPFC) using cluster-size correction within that mask (i.e., small-volume-corrected results). Whole-brain exploratory results are also reported. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are provided. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual tobacco advertisements as cues (visual stimuli), with a within-subject contrast (tobacco advertisement > control advertisement). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (whole-brain FDR-corrected maps and cluster thresholds; supporting tables/figures noted), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected evidence. Results are presented in figures and supporting tables (coordinates/ROI extracts), meeting allowance for reporting in tables/figures. Participant demographics (age, all male), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study used an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity paradigm with visual alcohol vs non-alcohol beverage images and reports group-level effects based on extracted percent signal change from an a priori right ventral striatum sphere (ROI) and subsequent GLM analyses. However, the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain results or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (no coordinates or voxelwise statistical maps/SVC reported). Therefore it meets the exclusion criterion for reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result (E3) and does not meet the required inclusion criterion for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result (I5). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant ALC>BEV contrast), I7 (participant and MRI details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group result), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise coordinates/figures/tables provided). Full text is complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given E3 is met, the study is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cannabis cues in cannabis-dependent adults. It reports within-subject voxelwise contrasts (cannabis cues > Gaussian baseline; cannabis > nature; cannabis > food) and whole-brain group-level analyses using SPM5 with cluster thresholds (voxelwise p<0.001, extent thresholding via AlphaSim to control FWE). Results are reported as clusters/regions with correlations to craving (tables/figures referenced). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are all described. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task study using visual cannabis-related, neutral, and positive images (visual cue component). It includes within-participant contrasts (cannabis vs neutral; cannabis vs baseline) and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume FWE-corrected coordinates (e.g., right amygdala x=36,4,-30 pFWE=0.006; thalamus/insula results). Core methodological details are provided (male participants age 18–30, 3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI with qualifying voxelwise SVC results. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI study using a visual alcohol cue-reactivity task (alcohol images vs soft-drink images) with a within-subject contrast (alcohol>soft drink). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (exploratory whole-brain SPM8 results with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE-corrected findings), and anatomically defined ROI analyses (amygdala/ventral striatum) are reported. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and SPM8 software, participant characteristics (male subjects, matched groups), and cue type. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (photographs). The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing food cues to control objects (e.g., fattening food > object, non-fattening food > object, fattening > non-fattening). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported using a region-of-interest voxelwise approach with cluster-thresholding corrections applied within anatomical masks (i.e., small-volume-corrected results) and coordinates/clusters are presented. Methods report participant age/sex (adult females), cue type (fattening vs non-fattening food images), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FLAME). Full text includes intro, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only without small-volume correction, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (water-related and drug-related pictures) in active heroin users. It reports within-subject contrasts (Thirst > Neutral and Drug > Neutral) analyzed at the group level using voxelwise SPM2 second-level one-sample t-tests, with voxelwise thresholds and Talairach coordinates reported. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are specified. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only results, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking cues presented in a block design. It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking>neutral (pre vs post and active vs sham), and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with stereotactic coordinates and t-values for whole-brain cluster findings (mOFC, NAc, ACC) and thresholding details. ROI analyses are also reported but whole-brain voxelwise results are present and meet the requirement for small-volume/voxelwise reporting. Methods report visual cue type, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8), and participant demographics. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food images > control images (separately for high- and low-calorie foods) and group-level voxelwise statistical results corrected for multiple comparisons (AlphaSim FWE cluster correction), with reported local maxima and figures/tables. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, AFNI for correction) are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue-exposure paradigm used tactile cues (presentation of a marijuana pipe vs a pencil) rather than visual-only or multimodal designs that include visual cues. The full text is otherwise complete and reports a within-participant marijuana>control contrast (I4), group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with cluster correction (I5), reports results in tables/figures (I6), and provides participant/cue/MRI/preprocessing details (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore exclusion is based specifically on failure to meet I3 (no visual cue component).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual images (COC) versus neutral images (NEU). It includes within-participant contrasts (COC > NEU) used in analyses and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FDR-corrected) based on that contrast. The paper provides necessary methodological details (participant ages/sex, 3.0T MRI field strength, preprocessing/software BrainVoyager). Although some voxelwise group comparisons returned null results, the presence of a group-level voxelwise task-evoked COC>NEU analysis satisfies the requirement. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI and is appropriate for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (450-s videos of craving-inducing and aversion-inducing alcohol scenes). The design includes within-participant contrasts (CIC vs mosaic control; AIC vs mosaic control) and group-level random-effects voxelwise GLM analyses producing SPMs with voxelwise FDR correction. Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts with statistics (p-values, FDR thresholds) and regional activations in the main text. MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager), participant demographics and cue types are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies with qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results and is suitable for inclusion.

The full text describes a BOLD fMRI study presenting visual marijuana-related cues vs matched non-drug visual cues in treatment-seeking, marijuana-dependent subjects. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (MJ cue > Non-MJ cue) at the group level and provides voxelwise results within an a priori ROI mask that were cluster-corrected via Monte Carlo simulation (i.e., small-volume-corrected). Coordinates are reported in tables and figures; participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are described. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This study is a resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) investigation with no task-based cue-reactivity paradigm or visual cues. Exclusion IDs met: E4 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without any task-evoked voxelwise results) and E5 (reports between-group contrasts and correlations but contains no within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion IDs met: none ([]). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no drug/natural reward cue-reactivity task with visual cues), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis objective of task-evoked visual cue-reactivity and must be excluded.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in smokers using visual smoking-related and matched neutral images (meets I3). The authors modeled within-subject event types (smoking vs non-smoking/neutral) and generated t-contrast images and random-effects (group-level) voxelwise analyses comparing cue conditions (meets I4). Results are reported as group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistics (SPM2 second-level random effects, uncorrected p<0.0001, cluster threshold, with reported activation clusters and a table; meets I5 and I6). Key methodological details are provided (participant sex, cue type, MRI field strength 1.5T, preprocessing and SPM2 software), satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text is incomplete (only abstract provided). The abstract confirms this is a functional MRI study using virtual-environment smoking cues, so inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity with a visual component) appears satisfied. However I cannot confirm key required criteria from the available text: I4 (presence of at least one within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus contrast) is not reported in the abstract; I5 (at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result) is not clearly reported—the abstract only mentions detected regions without specifying voxelwise/group-level/statistical reporting); I6 (reporting of voxelwise results in tables/figures/supplement) cannot be confirmed from the abstract; I7 (reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) is partially met (age described as "late-adolescent") but key MRI/method details are missing. Because full text is incomplete and essential inclusion criteria (I4 and I5) cannot be verified, I exclude the study pending access to the full article. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3. Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I4, I5, I6, I7.

The study includes a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with visual Prime stimuli (gain vs neutral) producing a within-participant anticipatory gain>neutral contrast (a natural reward-related cue>control contrast). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported, including small-volume–corrected activation in ventral striatum and dorsal ACC, satisfying voxelwise/SMC reporting requirements. Necessary participant/task details are provided, and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, or lack of within-subject cue>control contrast) are met. Therefore it is eligible for inclusion as a visual natural reward cue-reactivity study.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual heroin-related cues (images) in a cue-reactivity task and reports within-participant contrasts (heroin-related images > neutral images). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported (random-effects GLM, FDR-corrected whole-brain results, p<0.01, cluster extent threshold), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence. The paper provides participant demographics (male, ages reported), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug-related) cue-reactivity that used visual picture cues (and a taste) and reported within-subject voxelwise contrasts (alcohol > beverage; alcohol > visual control). Group-level random-effects SPM2 analyses are reported (thresholded maps, tables/figures with peak coordinates), and a small-volume ROI analysis of the ventral striatum is also presented. MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and SPM2 software, and participant demographics are described. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This fMRI study investigates drug cue processing with visual word stimuli (drug vs. matched neutral words) and reports within-participant drug>neutral contrasts and ROI analyses. However, the group-level voxelwise drug>neutral contrast did not reach whole-brain cluster-level corrected significance and no small-volume-corrected drug>neutral result is reported. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task>baseline effects (drug and neutral separately) and uncorrected voxelwise correlations and ROI findings, but it lacks a qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked drug>control result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) required by I5. Therefore it cannot be included in the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant drug vs. control contrasts were performed), I7 (participant and MRI details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise drug>control result). Exclusion applied: E3 (effectively only ROI/uncorrected voxelwise results for the key contrast). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-based task analyses and does not provide any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of a natural reward with a clear visual cue—the yellow light paired with juice), I4 (within-participant event contrasts comparing cue vs other event types), and I7 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical results are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded per E3.

This study is an event-related task fMRI investigation of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (heroin-related pictures vs neutral pictures). It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts (heroin > neutral) at the first level and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (within-group activations, between-group two-sample t-tests, and voxel-wise correlations) with cluster thresholds and MNI coordinates, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and cue type (visual pictures); participant inclusion/age range is stated and groups were demographically matched. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, or lacking within-participant cue>control contrasts) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related pictures versus neutral pictures, with within-participant (smoke>neutral) contrasts for both ‘crave’ and ‘resist’ conditions. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using FSL FEAT/FLAME with cluster correction (Z>2.3, cluster p=0.05) and results are reported in tables and figures (coordinates provided). Full text includes introduction, methods (participants, cues, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, statistical thresholds), results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, contains qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcohol images) and non-alcohol control images in young adult college students. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol vs. non-alcohol beverages and repetition effects (second vs first presentation). Whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses are reported with cluster-level correction (cluster extent threshold 8127 μl, p<.05) and results presented in tables/figures (coordinates and clusters in Table 3 and 4, Figures 2–5). Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual smoking and neutral images, with within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (group mPFC cluster with MNI coordinates and cluster-corrected p-value) and individual voxelwise hot-spot coordinates; results are presented with coordinates and statistical thresholds. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM5), and participant age/sex are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol-related pictures with a within-subject contrast (alcohol vs neutral). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (significant posterior cingulate cluster, thresholding and cluster extent reported) and provide methodological details (1.5T MRI, AFNI preprocessing/statistics, block-design visual cues). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study directly assesses alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol stimuli within a go/no-go task. It includes a within-participant contrast comparing alcohol cues to control stimuli (contrast 1: Alcohol_nogo > Non-alcohol_go) and additional interaction and main-effect contrasts. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates/tables/figures (SPM8; 3T scanner). Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and contains qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual drug cue reactivity.

This paper is a resting-state/seed-based functional connectivity study examining alexithymia, tobacco craving, and insula/ACC rsFC; it does not include any drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity task or visual cue paradigm, and it reports no within-participant cue>control task contrasts or task-evoked voxelwise results. Therefore it violates exclusion E4 (only seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without task-evoked voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), and I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked result) are not met. The full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). The manuscript does report participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing details, but these do not satisfy the core cue-reactivity/task-based requirements of the review. Outcome: EXCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual picture stimuli and includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol-associated versus control stimuli. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported (SPM99, threshold p<0.001 uncorrected, cluster-size reported) with tables/figures of regional activations. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting, and includes qualifying within-participant contrasts).

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study presents smoking-related versus neutral visual cues and reports within-participant contrasts (smoking>neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses (three-way ANOVA) with reported peak coordinates and SPM maps. MRI field strength (3.0 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported, participant characteristics (male smokers, ages summarized) and cue types are described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Full text is not accessible (page unavailable); only title/metadata are available. Unable to verify whether the study is a functional MRI task with visual cues, whether it includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, or whether it reports qualifying voxelwise (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) group-level results. Therefore I cannot apply required inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, or I6. No exclusion criteria can be confirmed from the available information. Because the core article content (methods/results) is missing, fulltext_incomplete is set to true and the study must be excluded from the review at this screening stage pending retrieval of the full text.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cocaine-related pictures and a blocked cue task, with within-subject contrasts computed (Cocaine > Neutral) for each session. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed using SPM8 with ROI small-volume FWE-corrected results reported (e.g., VTA/SN FWE-corrected), and coordinates/t-values are presented in the text. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant details are reported. Thus the study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for visual cue-based fMRI cue-reactivity with qualifying voxelwise results. Full text is complete.

This is an fMRI study of visual smoking cues with within-subject contrasts (smoking vs neutral) in nicotine-deprived smokers, but the analyses are performed using predefined region-of-interest (ROI) approaches and report ROI-based percent signal changes rather than group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Therefore it fails the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise group analysis. Exclusion ID met: E3 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI study of drug-related visual cue-reactivity), I4 (within-participant contrast drug cues > control stimuli), I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing details reported). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical result reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an fMRI investigation using visual cue videos (food and cocaine) in human participants and reports within-subject contrasts (cocaine>neutral and food>neutral). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed with SPM8 and cluster-level FWE correction; results are reported with cluster tables/coordinates and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (4T), cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is a human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that used visual stimuli (pictorial cues) within a multimodal design (visual + auditory). It employed within-subject contrasts (high-ED and low-ED food cues vs. neutral nonfood cues and high-ED>low-ED comparisons) at the group level. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM5 and results are reported as statistical maps, figures, and a coordinate table (Table 1) with cluster-correction procedures described. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM5) are reported. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) with a within-participant contrast of ‘favourite drinks > neutral’ reported. The paper reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain: P<0.001 uncorrected) and small-volume-corrected ROI results (P<0.05 SVC/FDR) with coordinates. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity using a clear visual cue (milkshake image) that signaled delivery of tastants. It includes a within-participant cue contrast (anticipatory milkshake cue > anticipatory tasteless-solution cue) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (cluster-level q-FDR <0.05 across gray-matter-masked whole brain). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI scanner, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, DARTEL), and the full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical), and the provided full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in nicotine-dependent humans using visual smoking-related cues vs matched neutral images (meets I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral during encoding and retrieval (meets I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with whole-brain cluster correction (Z=2.3, p<0.05) and reported coordinates/tables/figures (meets I5 and I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics (FSL) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state-only (E4), and include within-subject cue>control contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts (E5). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion basis: No qualifying within-participant visual cue > control contrast was reported. (a) Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 strictly apply. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study with clear visual cues: visual words 'Alcohol' and 'Water' presented), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported for taste/PE contrasts), I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures/supplement), I7 (reported participant demographics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 was not satisfied — the paper does not report a within-participant contrast of visual drug cue > control cue (analyses and reported results focus on taste/outcome contrasts and prediction-error effects rather than cue>control visual cue contrasts). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the cue-reactivity meta-analysis and is excluded.

This study used alcohol taste delivery (gustatory cues) as the primary alcohol cue (alcohol vs isocaloric control litchi juice). Although participants also viewed written CT/CCT statements, the reward-related cue-elicitation was via taste rather than visual alcohol cues. Therefore it does not meet I3 (clear visual cue component for drug/natural reward cue-reactivity). The study does meet I4 (within-participant alcohol>control cue contrasts), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with cluster correction), I6 (coordinates and figures reported), and I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/statistics). No exclusion criteria were triggered (none of E3–E6 apply). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study that used visual stimuli (pictures) for gambling (natural reward) and smoking (drug) cues and included within-subject contrasts (gambling>neutral; smoking>neutral). Group-level voxelwise statistical results are reported with cluster-wise family-wise error correction and coordinate information; figures and tables of activations are described. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing (SPM2) and participant demographics (all-male, Ns), satisfying reporting preferences. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or absence of within-subject cue>control contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a single-case fMRI report (one alcohol-dependent participant) using visual alcohol cues and reporting within-participant alcohol vs non-alcohol contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study with visual alcohol cues) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast). However, the study does not provide group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (no group analyses or small-volume-corrected, voxelwise group results), so I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly triggered, but failure to meet I5 is sufficient for exclusion. Full text appears complete. Exclusion reason: lack of qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (I5 not met).

This study directly investigates fMRI cue-reactivity to cannabis-related visual word stimuli (cannabis word Stroop) and reports within-participant contrasts of cannabis-related words > neutral words. Group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction are reported (peak coordinates and pFWE values for ROIs, e.g., insula, amygdala, ventral striatum), satisfying the requirement for qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results. The paradigm uses visual cues, includes the necessary within-subject contrast, and provides MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (pornography/erotic) cue-reactivity using visual cues and an event-related incentive delay task. The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing erotic cue conditions to control/other cue types and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results within a priori ventral striatum ROIs that survived small-volume FWE correction (PSVC-FWE<0.05). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and analysis tools (MATLAB, MarsBaR, WFU PickAtlas, SPSS mentioned) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: the study does not rely solely on ROI-only uncorrected analyses, nor only connectivity/resting-state, nor lacks within-subject cue>control contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes clear visual stimuli (multimodal visual + auditory) and reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie (reward) > low-calorie (control) food cues. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (SPM5; cluster-extent threshold with p<0.05 corrected) and results/t-maps/clusters are described, meeting the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant/sample and MRI acquisition/processing details are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study using visual cues (game screenshots and smoking images) to elicit cue-reactivity for both a natural reward (gaming) and a drug (nicotine). The design includes within-participant contrasts (gaming>neutral and smoking>neutral) at first level and group-level voxelwise analyses. Group results were reported with whole-brain FDR-corrected maps for within-group activations and small-volume-corrected (SVC) group comparisons and conjunction analyses in predefined ROIs (SPM5), fulfilling the requirement for qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject ALC>BEV contrasts, but all reported neuroimaging results are ROI-based (average timecourses from a priori spheres) rather than group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one qualifying voxelwise result (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (heroin-related pictures vs neutral pictures). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of heroin-related > neutral cues and presents group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses (two-sample t-tests) with multiple-comparison correction (AFNI Alphasim), with results described in tables/figures and coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant demographics. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task-evoked visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). The study includes within-participant contrasts of food>non-food at first level, and group-level voxelwise inference using FSL RANDOMISE (TFCE, FWE-corrected) within predefined masks (small-volume approach), with cluster peaks and MNI coordinates reported. Participant age range, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT, ICA-AROMA, RANDOMISE) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and within-subject heroin-related vs. neutral contrasts. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (paired t-tests) with coordinates/clusters and ROI follow-up, meeting the requirement for a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result. Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue type, 1.5T MRI, preprocessing/statistical software SPM2). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to visual drug rewards.

This study used a simulated slot-machine task (visual gambling cues) to examine reward anticipation and near-miss processing in pathological gambling and cocaine dependence. It does not investigate drug-related cues or prototypical natural-reward cues as defined by the review objective, and the within-participant contrasts are between gambling-related task events (e.g., possible-reward vs certain-loss, near-miss vs full-loss) rather than drug-cue>control or natural-reward-cue>control contrasts. Therefore it fails to meet I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast for drug or natural reward cues). The paper does report whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-level FWE) and provides results in text/figures and participant/method details, satisfying I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are applicable. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I3 and I4 are not met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity that includes an explicit visual cue component (orange triangle/blue star signaling impending chocolate milk vs tasteless solution). It reports within-subject contrasts (anticipation chocolate milk > anticipation tasteless solution; receipt chocolate milk > receipt tasteless solution) at the group level using voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses (SPM8) with small-volume correction in a priori ROIs and whole-brain thresholding; results are reported with coordinates/tables (S2–S4). MRI field strength (3.0 T) and preprocessing/statistics are described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental tables are referenced. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of nicotine-dependent smokers using visual smoking cues. The paradigm used visual-only smoking-related pictures (I3). Within-subject contrasts were constructed (smoke and neutral vs rest), and the paper reports a group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analysis for the contrast smoke cue vs rest (reported in text/figures; p≤0.005 uncorrected), satisfying the requirement for a task-evoked voxelwise result (I4, I5, I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (TBV, SPM8) are reported (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual word cues (drug vs. neutral words presented via MRI goggles). It reports within-participant contrasts (drug-word vs. neutral-word) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain cluster-level correction and small-volume corrections (coordinates and statistics presented in Table 1 and figures). MRI field strength (4T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are described. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain/SVC results), I6 (results reported in tables/figures), and I7 (participant and acquisition details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs neutral pictures) in within-subject block and event-related paradigms. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) at the group level, with voxelwise whole-brain analyses and cluster-correction (AlphaSim), and provides MNI coordinates and figures/tables for significant clusters. Key methodological details are reported (participants’ age range and sex distribution, cue type, 3T MRI, preprocessing/statistics using SPM8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s core content requirement for cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward visual cues. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction and cluster correction), I6 (voxelwise results are described and available in text/figures), I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (fMRI task is a Monetary Incentive Delay task assessing monetary reward processing, not drug cue or natural reward visual cue-reactivity), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control — contrasts are monetary reward vs neutral). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because it does not address drug or natural reward visual cue-reactivity required by the meta-analysis.

Only the abstract and metadata are available (fulltext_incomplete=true). The abstract indicates an fMRI task with a visual heroin cue and within-subject activation reporting, so inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component) and I4 (within-participant drug-cue>control contrast) appear satisfied. However, the available content is insufficient to verify I5: that at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) is reported (no coordinates, tables, or clear statement of whole-brain/SVC voxelwise results in the abstract). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are demonstrably met. Because the full text (methods, full results, tables/figures) is not provided, I cannot confirm I5; therefore the study must be excluded pending retrieval of the complete article for verification.

The full text is a peer-reviewed empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues and neutral control images, with a within-subject contrast (smoking cues > neutral) analyzed at the group level using voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses. Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and tables of coordinates (figures and tables), satisfying requirements for task-evoked voxelwise results. The paper provides participant age/sex (10 males, mean age 32), cue type (visual smoking stimuli), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM99). The full article includes methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Full text appears incomplete: only acknowledgments and references are provided, core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is missing. Therefore I cannot verify required inclusion criteria. No inclusion criteria can be confirmed. Specifically: I3 (fMRI study with visual cues) — title suggests visual food cues but not verifiable from text provided; I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast) — not reported in available content; I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC results) — not reported; I6 (reporting of voxelwise results in tables/figures/supplement) — not available. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confidently applied given the incomplete text. Recommendation: obtain the complete full text to assess eligibility.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues and a within-subject contrast (alcohol > neutral). The manuscript reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain cluster results) and also region-of-interest small-volume-corrected (SVC, FWE) results for a priori regions; results are reported in tables/figures. Methods provide MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and SPM5, and participant demographics (n=38, mean age and range). Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity, a within-participant cue>control contrast, and qualifying voxelwise whole-brain and SVC results. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original human fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) in an implicit approach-avoidance task, directly addressing cue-reactivity. The analysis includes within-subject contrasts that compare alcohol versus soft-drink control stimuli within the approach/avoid framework (interaction and separate approach>avoid contrasts reported). Group-level voxelwise results are reported and corrected using small-volume correction (SVC) with FWE (p<0.05) in a priori ROIs (NAcc, mPFC, amygdala), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked statistical results. Methods report participant age/sex information, cue type, 3T field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI analyses without voxelwise SVC, connectivity-only analyses, or lack of within-participant cue>control contrast) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This full-text reports an empirical 1.5T fMRI study using visual alcohol-drinking video cues and a mosaic control, with within-participant contrasts (alcohol vs mosaic) and group-level voxelwise GLM/RFX results (clusters reported with FDR correction and tabulated coordinates). Methods include MRI field strength, preprocessing, and analysis software (BrainVoyager), and participant demographics are described. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation using visual heroin-related cues (pictorial block design) and reports a within-participant contrast (heroin-related > neutral). Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted using FSL/FLAME with whole-brain cluster correction (z threshold and cluster probability) and results are described in tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked statistical results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation using visual food images (natural rewards) with within-participant contrasts (appetizing > non-foods and appetizing > bland) and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction in striatal ROIs. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/software (SPM5), and participant details are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies and provides qualifying small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract provided). Abstract indicates the study used visual movie cues (a 'heroin puffing' movie), so I3 (visual cue component) appears satisfied. However the provided content does NOT allow verification of I4 (a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli) or I5 (reporting of at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result). I6 cannot be confirmed because no tables/figures/coordinates or methods/results sections are available. I7 (reporting of participant details and MRI methods) cannot be verified. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be positively identified from the abstract alone. Because the full text is incomplete and key methodological/results details are missing, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is a human task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-subject contrasts (food > object) and reports group-level voxelwise activation maps for the FOOD contrast (Fasted-Initial visit) used to define ROIs. The paper describes imaging acquisition (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), participant demographics, and provides task-evoked voxelwise results (whole-brain group activation maps), satisfying the requirement for at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Although between-visit voxelwise corrected differences were non-significant and much of the main inference used ROI-extracted values, the presence of group-level voxelwise activation maps for the food>object contrast meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity that includes visual stimuli and reports qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results at the group level. Evidence: (1) Visual cues (pictures of alcohol) were presented (multimodal design including visual cues). (2) Within-participant contrasts (alcohol pictures vs control pictures and the opposites) were modeled and examined. (3) Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted (mixed-effects), with results converted to Z-scores and cluster-wise FWE correction reported (cluster-wide p<0.05 FWE over the whole brain), satisfying whole-brain/small-volume-corrected reporting. (4) Required methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software FSL). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visually presented cocaine-related words (cocaine-word Stroop). The paper reports within-participant cocaine>neutral contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise analyses (family-wise error correction p<.05) and additionally uses small-volume (IFG) analyses, with significant clusters reported. Methods include 3T scanner details and preprocessing/statistical software (CamBA/SPM), and participant demographics are reported. Thus it satisfies I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant drug cues>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain and small-volume-corrected results), I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures), and I7 (key methodological details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study used ASL fMRI with cocaine-related video cues (visual stimuli) but did not report a within-participant voxelwise task-evoked cue>control contrast. The analyses focused on seed-based functional connectivity (amygdala whole-brain regression) and wavelet transform coherence (WTC) of CBF time series, not on task-evoked activation maps (drug cues > control) at the group voxelwise level. Therefore it fails to meet the required within-subject cue>control contrast and qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result. Exclusion criteria applied: E4 (study reports seed-based connectivity/WTC without an accompanying qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) and E5 (no within-participant cue>control contrast presented). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (used visual cocaine-related video cues) and I7 (reported participant characteristics and MRI details). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control contrast) and I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (movie scenes). It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking versus matched control scenes, and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise results (thresholded maps and a table of coordinates). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI cue-reactivity and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

Full text is complete. Exclusion decision because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it does not include a visual cue component. The experiment used gustatory (milkshake tasted via gustometer) stimuli (milkshake vs tasteless solution) rather than visual reward cues. Met inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrast milkshake>tasteless), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain cluster-corrected results reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported with coordinates/figures), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded solely because I3 (visual cue component) is not satisfied; the meta-analysis objective requires visual cue-reactivity studies.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual smoking cues (photographs) and control images, meeting I3. The authors computed a within-participant smoking cue > control cue contrast and entered these contrast images into group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2), with results reported as whole-brain voxelwise maps, tables of coordinates, and figures, satisfying I4, I5, and I6. The Methods report MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM2), and participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type, satisfying I7. The paper is empirical and provides whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise group results (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only), so no exclusion criteria (E3–E5) apply. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue reactivity with visual cues and a within-participant SCs vs NCs contrast, and group-level voxelwise statistical maps reported with peak coordinates. However, all reported voxelwise analyses were conducted within an a priori anatomical mask (WFU PickAtlas) and reported at an uncorrected threshold (P<0.001) without applying small-volume correction (SVC) or reporting whole-brain corrected results. Therefore the study effectively reports ROI/mask-restricted results without a qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise result, which meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I6 (voxelwise results/coordinates reported), I7 (participant and methods details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise result). Full text is complete.

This full text reports an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol cues (handling, pouring, smelling favorite alcoholic drink) and a task contrast of alcohol cues > neutral/control. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (whole-brain contrasts, coordinates, cluster sizes, p-values, and supplementary tables/figures). The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (not a truncated abstract). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical).

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-based task analyses and does not provide a group-level voxelwise (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) task-evoked result required for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual smoking cues used), I4 (within-participant smoke>rest contrasts/PSC), I7 (participant demographics, cue type, field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected analysis reported). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study of heroin (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images). It reports within-subjects Heroin>Neutral contrasts and voxelwise group-level whole-brain analyses (random-effects two-sample t-tests) with FDR correction and coordinates reported. Methods (3T scanner, SPM8, preprocessing, task design) and results (whole-brain activations and coordinate reporting) are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is excluded because it does not include a visual cue component required by I3. It used olfactory (ethanol odor) stimulation rather than visual cues. The full text is complete and the study does meet other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrast: ethanol odor > neutral air), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain fMRI results reported), I6 (voxelwise results presented in figures/tables), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Inclusion IDs met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (visual cue component). Exclusion IDs met: none.

This is an fMRI task study using visual cues (novel geometric CS) paired with alcohol infusion, meeting the review focus on visual drug-related cue-reactivity. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of CS+ (alcohol-paired) vs CS− (saline-paired) (the CS+>CS− contrast was explicitly tested, albeit yielding no significant positive clusters) and reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain results (the reverse contrast CS−>CS+ produced FWE-corrected cluster-level results). Methods report MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistics (SPM5), and participant demographics are provided. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Although the CS+>CS− contrast produced null findings, the requisite within-participant voxelwise analysis was performed and reported, satisfying inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an event-related fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual heroin-related vs neutral pictures and includes a within-subject contrast (heroin > neutral). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (peak coordinates and t-values; P<0.001 uncorrected) and used to define a PCC seed. Relevant methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, 3T MRI field strength, SPM5 preprocessing). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (the study is not ROI-only, not only resting-state/connectivity, and provides qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results). Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of drug (tobacco) cue-reactivity using visual smoking images. It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral images and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects GLM and mixed-effects ANCOVA) with voxelwise thresholding and cluster-level correction (p<0.05). Results are reported in the text and tables/figures. Participant characteristics (adult women), cue type (visual smoking images), MRI field strength (Siemens Trio 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX and preprocessing steps) are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes qualifying within-subject contrast). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a monetary incentive delay task with visual cues signaling gain vs nongain (within-participant contrasts of reward>control). Group-level voxelwise results are reported including small-volume-corrected (SVC) ROI analyses (pFWE<.05) and whole-brain FWE-corrected results for key contrasts. Participant demographics and scanning/method details are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study using visual cannabis cues (images) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<.05) with sufficient methodological detail (age/sex summary, 3T field, FSL preprocessing). However, the paper does not report a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast (e.g., cannabis > neutral) as required by I4. The primary reported contrast is an approach-bias contrast (approach-block > avoid-block) and condition>baseline contrasts, but no explicit cannabis>control voxelwise contrast is presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I4. Exclusion criteria applied: E5. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) with visual cues and reports whole-brain, FWE-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results (figures/tables), and reports participant demographics and MRI details. Therefore it satisfies I3, I5, I6, and I7. However, the paper does not present a clear within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., food > non-food) at the group level that would qualify as a cue-reactivity contrast; the reported voxelwise results focus on glycemic-condition contrasts (euglycemia vs hypoglycemia) and condition×task interactions rather than an explicit food>non-food within-subject cue>control contrast. Because it lacks the required within-participant cue>control analysis, it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Thus it must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking cues (cue-reactivity task with smoking-related pictures vs neutral) and reports within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts. The paper provides whole-brain, cluster-wise corrected voxelwise results (cluster-wise thresholding using Monte Carlo simulation/3dClustSim) and shows brain maps/contrast results and coordinates, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only (it includes task-evoked whole-brain results), and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual images and an incidental food vs. non-food within-participant contrast. The paper reports ROI analyses but explicitly states that group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses of food>non-food were conducted (reported in Supplementary material), which satisfies the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result (I5) and is allowable per I6. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

Exclusion E3 applies: the manuscript reports only ROI-based analyses (averaged beta values for nucleus accumbens and caudate putamen) and follow-up GLMs on ROI data; no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts are reported, so inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (fMRI of reward-related cues using a visual Monetary Incentive Delay task), I4 (within-participant reward>neutral contrasts), I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength 3T, and preprocessing/statistics software SPM5 reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of natural-reward (high-calorie food) cue-reactivity using exclusively visual stimuli, reports within-subject contrasts (high-calorie > non-food; high-calorie > low-calorie), and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (Z>2.3, p<0.05 corrected). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), imaging parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, SPSS) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual food cues (HC vs LC pictures) in obese participants pre- and post-laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. It includes within-participant HC>LC contrasts, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-level FWE-corrected, P_FWE<0.05) with results described in the main text and supplementary materials, and provides MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective (natural reward visual cue-reactivity) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used resting-state fMRI (ICA and ACC-seed rsFC) to examine neural correlates of nicotine withdrawal and withdrawal-induced craving; there was no task presenting visual drug or natural reward cues and no within-participant cue>control (visual) contrast. Thus it does not address cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity results. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports only seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an fMRI cue-reactivity task with visual cues), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control contrast), I5 (no group-level task-evoked voxelwise results), I6 (not applicable — no qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of a natural reward (chocolate) that includes a clear visual cue condition (picture of chocolate) and multimodal conditions. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of visual cue > control (chocpic vs grey control) and related contrasts, and presents group-level voxelwise SPM results with small-volume corrections and peak coordinates. Methods report participant demographics (female, age 20–30), cue types, 3.0 T scanner, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual monetary reward cues ($ vs #) during an antisaccade task, meeting the review focus on drug or natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity. The study reports within-participant contrasts (Reward vs Neutral) and analyzes reward>neutral effects. Group-level mixed-effects fMRI analyses were run and z-statistic images within a priori ROIs were corrected for multiple comparisons using FDR (i.e., small-volume correction within ROIs), satisfying the requirement for a voxelwise, small-volume-corrected task-evoked result. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, FSL). Whole-brain analyses found no clusters beyond ROIs, but that does not negate the reported small-volume voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion.

This study used an fMRI Monetary Incentive Delay Task to examine reward/loss processing with monetary cues, not drug cues or prototypical natural reward cues (e.g., food, erotic stimuli). Inclusion: I5 is satisfied (group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction and reported coordinates), I6 is satisfied (coordinates and ROI results reported in main text/tables), and I7 is satisfied (participant demographics and methodological details reported). Exclusion: none of E3–E6 apply. Not satisfied: I3 (study does not assess drug- or clearly defined natural reward-related cue-reactivity; stimuli are monetary task cues rather than drug or natural-reward cue images) and I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control as required by the review scope). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet the review’s scope for drug or natural reward cue-reactivity and is excluded.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs. neutral images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral), group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with explicit thresholding and cluster correction (AlphaSim/FWE) and reports regional activations (peaks/ROIs). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM5/SPM8) and task details are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol and non-alcohol beverage images (meets I3). It includes within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral beverage cues (ALC-BEV) (meets I4). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with FWE cluster-correction and peak coordinates (meets I5 and I6). The manuscript provides participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) details (meets I7). The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are applicable. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking videos as cues (I3). It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking>control videos (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported with multiple-comparisons correction (whole-brain corrected and a priori small-volume correction for DLPFC) and coordinate tables/figures (I5, I6). Participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (fmristat), and cue type are reported (I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based task analyses and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of drug cue reactivity using visual smoking cues), I4 (within-participant comparisons of smoking cues vs control cues), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level task result reported). Full text appears complete and contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related pictorial cues and neutral control images, with within-participant contrasts (smoking-related > neutral) reported. The paper provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain cluster-corrected statistics (Z>2.3, cluster p<.05) for SR vs N contrasts in smokers, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. ROI analyses of the ventral striatum are also reported. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is an original human fMRI study). Full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore, the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual picture cues (alcohol, marijuana, polydrug, and IAPS emotional pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral (e.g., alcohol>neutral, polydrug>neutral, marijuana>neutral). Analyses were performed as group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistics using FSL/FEAT (mixed-effects OLS) with results presented in tables and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3T Siemens Allegra), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual alcohol, polydrug and marijuana picture cues and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise BOLD contrasts (meeting I3, I5, I6, and I7), the reported analyses contrast non-studied versus studied items within the same drug cue categories rather than a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast (e.g., drug > neutral or non-drug).
