The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study does evaluate natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity and reports within-subject contrasts and group-level voxelwise results, but the cues are gustatory (oral delivery of a palatable drink) rather than visual. Inclusion criterion I3 (clear visual cue component) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant palatable stimulus > purified water contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures/tables), and I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present) so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because the meta-analysis specifically requires a visual cue component, this study must be excluded.

This study does not assess fMRI visual cue-reactivity contrasts. Although it is an empirical fMRI study in substance-dependent participants and reports whole-brain voxelwise TMS-evoked BOLD results, the measured task is TMS-evoked activity (interleaved TMS/BOLD) and cTBS effects, not a within-participant drug-cue > control visual stimulus contrast. Exclusion ID met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength, and analysis software reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no clear fMRI visual cue-reactivity paradigm), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control contrast), I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result for cue-reactivity). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of high-caloric food). It includes within-participant contrasts (Food > Neutral) at the group level (one-sample t tests and group comparisons). The paper reports voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain FWE-corrected statistics for exploratory analyses (Food > Neutral occipital activation) and ROI analyses with coordinate reporting; preprocessing and analysis software (SPM2), MRI field strength (1.5 T), participant sex (female) and cue type are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the fMRI task used olfactory (food and non-food odor) cues rather than a visual cue component required by the meta-analysis. It does satisfy I4 (within-participant food>non-food odor contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected result in vmPFC with FWE correction), I6 (voxelwise results reported), and I7 (participant demographics and scanning details reported). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because it lacks the required visual cue modality (I3 not met).

This study does not assess visual cue–reactivity or task-evoked cue>control contrasts required for the meta-analysis. It reports resting-state measures (ALFF) and seed-based functional connectivity before and after ingestion and group comparisons, but no task-based visual cue paradigm or within-participant cue>control contrast. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 (reports only seed-based/connectivity or resting-state analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) applies. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no visual cue component), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), and I5 (no task-evoked whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results). No inclusion criteria are satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Excluded because the study reports only resting-state fMRI and TMS/behavioral results and does not report any task-evoked, voxelwise cue>control fMRI contrasts required for cue-reactivity meta-analysis. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (not a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity study — fMRI data are resting-state, not cue-evoked), I4 (no within-participant cue>control task contrast reported), I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (no qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results in tables/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete and was assessed in full.

Full text is complete. Although the study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual erotic (natural) and monetary cues and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked results, it does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast for natural reward-related visual cues (the authors modeled anticipation but report outcome-phase results and did not present cue>control cue-reactivity analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cues for natural rewards present/assessed), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures/tables), I7 (participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control cue-reactivity contrast reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I4.

The study includes visual natural reward cues (erotica) and reports within-participant contrasts comparing erotica vs neutral (box-car models). Group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses were performed (random-effects, whole-brain analyses using SPM8) and voxelwise results are reported. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual natural reward cue-reactivity with qualifying voxelwise group results. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an event-related fMRI experiment of monetary reward expectation using visual instruction cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast: reward vs no-reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does NOT assess drug-related or natural reward-related cue-reactivity — it uses monetary/secondary rewards, which fall outside the meta-analysis target of drug or natural reward cues). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided). Therefore excluded for failing I3.

This is an fMRI study using the Monetary Incentive Delay Task (visual monetary cues) probing natural reward-related cue-reactivity, with group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported (family-wise error-corrected whole-brain analyses). The paper reports within-participant task contrasts related to anticipation of monetary reward (A2Win/A2Loss phases) and their Scan2–Scan1 differences and presents voxelwise coordinates/tables and figures. These satisfy the review focus on visual natural reward cue-reactivity and the requirement for voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results. Full methods, results, and ROI analyses are present in the article text provided; core preprocessing/statistical software and participant data are reported. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (monetary) processing using visual cues (cards/arrows) and includes within-participant contrasts of reward anticipation > baseline and reward outcome > baseline. Group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-level correction (AlphaSim) across pre-specified ROIs and MNI coordinates are provided (i.e., qualifying voxelwise/small-volume-corrected results). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue-related natural reward task, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and group-level voxelwise results. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a pre-registered randomized trial protocol that describes an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity paradigm using visual alcohol images on a 3T scanner and details preprocessing (SPM12/MATLAB). However, the manuscript is a protocol with no reported empirical fMRI results or group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts. It therefore does not provide the required within-participant drug-cue > control contrast analyses nor any whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results required for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study of monetary (natural) reward using visually presented stimuli (card-guessing task) that includes a within-participant contrast of reward anticipation>baseline (a cue>control contrast) and reward outcome>baseline. Group-level voxelwise results are reported within an anatomically defined ventral striatum ROI with small-volume/FWE correction and peak coordinates provided. The paper reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Thus it meets I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast in anticipation), I5 (small-volume-corrected voxelwise group results), I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures), and I7 (participant/MRI/method details). It does not meet any exclusion criteria: results are not ROI-only without voxelwise correction (small-volume correction applied), not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and not only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not report a qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). Exclusion criterion E3 is met: analyses are ROI-based (ROI eigenvariate extraction and genotype-ROI regressions) and no voxelwise SVC or whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/coordinates are presented for the MID task. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related cues—the MID task uses visual reward/loss cues), I4 (within-participant condition contrasts such as A1 L5 phase were analyzed), I6 (results are reported in figures/tables), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result is provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cues (MID task: cue shapes signaling reward vs neutral), assessing natural reward-related cue-reactivity (monetary reward). It includes a within-participant contrast of reward versus neutral anticipation (reward>neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (group activation maps and voxelwise SPM5 two-sample tests thresholded at p<0.05 FWE corrected). Results are presented in text, figures and ROI follow-ups. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. Full text contains Intro, Methods, Results, Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study of food rewards uses visual food cues (images) and includes a within-participant contrast of high‑palatable food > plain food, reported as voxelwise, group‑level task-evoked results. Analyses were conducted with SPM8 and a reward‑system mask (Neurosynth) with cluster‑extent correction (AlphaSim) within that mask, providing small‑volume corrected voxelwise results and reporting coordinates/figures. The study therefore meets the review focus on natural reward visual cue‑reactivity and satisfies key inclusion criteria (visual cue component, within‑subject cue>control contrast, and group‑level voxelwise (SVC) results). Core methods and results (participants, MRI field strength 3.0T, preprocessing/statistics software, task contrasts) are reported in the full text. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence, include for the meta‑analysis.

This study does not meet the review’s scope and voxelwise reporting requirements. It used a Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task with geometric cues signaling monetary reward/loss (secondary rewards), not drug cues or typical natural reward images; therefore I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues) is not met. Although within-participant contrasts of cue>neutral (e.g., high reward>neutral, high loss>neutral) are reported (I4 met) and required reporting details (age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are present (I7 met), the fMRI results are reported as ROI-based percent-signal-change analyses in the bilateral Nucleus Accumbens with no whole-brain voxelwise or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise statistical maps or coordinates provided. That violates inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food photographs) and non-food control images, meeting the review focus. It includes within-participant contrasts of food>non-food (cue>control) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects paired-sample t-tests and ANOVA) with multiple-comparison correction. Voxelwise results are presented in figures and supplemental tables. Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing details are reported. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (high-calorie images) vs non-food objects in a within-subject, randomized crossover design. It reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie food > non-food objects) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results: a primary small-volume/ROI-confirmatory VTA analysis and an exploratory whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis (reported with coordinates and cluster tables). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports only task-modulated seed-based connectivity (PPI) results relating VS connectivity to reward anticipation (Big-win > No-win) in adolescent smokers, without reporting a standalone task-evoked within-participant voxelwise activation contrast (natural reward cue > control) as a qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected activation result. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual reward cues in the MID task), I4 (within-participant contrast of reward cue vs no-reward cue: Big-win > No-win), and I7 (reports participant demographics and methodological details). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying task-evoked voxelwise activation result reported independent of connectivity analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used resting-state fMRI and an observed eating-in-the-absence-of-hunger behavioral paradigm; it did not present or contrast visual drug or natural reward cues. Exclusion criterion E4 applies: the paper reports only resting-state/ICA and seed-based connectivity analyses without any task-evoked cue>control voxelwise contrast. Inclusion criterion I7 (reporting of participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) is satisfied. Inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity with visual cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), and I5 (task-evoked whole-brain or SVC voxelwise results) are not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of natural reward cues (food) that includes a clear visual cue component (appetizing vs unappetizing food images). The study reports within-participant contrasts of appetizing>unappetizing food images and milkshake cue contrasts, and conducts group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with coordinates and FWE-corrected thresholds. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without within-subject cue>control contrast, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the task uses gustatory (taste) stimuli (sucrose and water) rather than a clear visual cue component. It does, however, include within-participant tastant contrasts (sucrose vs water) and voxelwise small-volume-corrected task-evoked results, and reports coordinates and methodological details. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant natural reward-related contrast examined), I5 (small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results), I6 (results reported in figures/tables), I7 (participant and MRI details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (visual cue component). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses a Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task measuring reward anticipation (large vs small win contrast) rather than a cue-reactivity paradigm to drug or natural reward stimuli. While it reports voxelwise, group-level fMRI results with coordinates (satisfying I5) and presents results in figures/tables (I6), it does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual reward/drug cues as defined by the review (I3 not met). The primary reported within-subject contrast is ‘large win vs small win’ (reward anticipation), not a cue>control contrast of drug or natural reward cues (I4 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are directly triggered, but failure to meet I3 and I4 prevents inclusion. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) and monetary cues in a modified monetary incentive delay task. It reports within-participant contrasts (erotic>neutral; monetary>neutral) for anticipation and outcome phases. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain family-wise error correction and ROI small-volume correction for the ventral striatum. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, MRI field strength 3T, preprocessing SPM12) and task/cue descriptions are provided in the main text with figures and tables. These features satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and qualifying voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material not required for eligibility.

Although this is an empirical fMRI task study that reports voxelwise, group-level task-evoked results (whole-brain thresholding and reported coordinates), includes within-participant contrasts of reward anticipation/outcome, and provides participant/sample and acquisition/preprocessing details, it does NOT investigate drug cues or natural reward-related cues. The task uses monetary incentives (monetary incentive delay), a secondary/extrinsic reward, rather than drug-related or natural reward cues (e.g., food, sexual, social). Therefore it fails the core content inclusion criteria I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue component) and I4 (within-participant drug>control or natural reward>control contrast as required). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met. Because key inclusion criteria (I3 and I4) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it reports primarily between-group contrasts (BEpost-tx vs NBEpost-tx) and does not present an explicit within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., reward-cue > neutral-cue) required for cue-reactivity meta-analysis (Exclusion E5). Met inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI with clear visual cues in the MIDT), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported with correction), I6 (voxelwise results available in tables/figures), and I7 (reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics). Did not meet I4 (no clear within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used a monetary incentive delay task with explicit visual cues (monetary symbols and amounts) and reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., gain vs. no-gain anticipation and outcomes). The paper provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses including a post-hoc whole-brain analysis with cluster correction (AFNI 3dttest++/Clustsim) and reports activation maps/clusters, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected results. Participant details, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-groups-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is a within-subject fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood (food vs. nonfood) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise paired t-tests (clusterwise FDR-corrected results reported: IFG and vmPFC surviving q<0.05). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural (food) reward cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (images of milkshake and water). It includes within-participant contrasts (anticipated milkshake > anticipated tasteless solution; milkshake intake > tasteless solution). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were reported with cluster-wise correction (P < 0.05 corrected) and stereotactic coordinates in Table 2; additionally, a more-sensitive ROI (striatum) analysis was performed. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T Allegra), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, AFNI tools described) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural (food) reward processing using an incentive delay task with explicit visual cues (basket/wallet images) cueing potential reward. The study reports within-participant contrasts contrasting anticipation of high reward versus no-reward (anticipation_high) and receipt_high versus no-receipt, i.e., cue>control contrasts. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (results reported at voxelwise P<0.001 uncorrected, with tables/figures and MNI coordinates). The paper provides participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8), and task/cue details. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used visual cues (images of close others) and within-subject contrasts (close other vs stranger and vs serial subtraction), and reports participant demographics and imaging details. However, all neuroimaging results are reported from an a priori anatomical ROI (ventral striatum) using extracted parameter estimates and ANOVAs; no whole-brain voxelwise or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting) and does not meet I5/I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results).

This fMRI study assesses natural reward-related cue-reactivity (social and monetary rewards) using clear visual cues (graphical monetary cues, wallet images, and pictures of smiling faces). Within-participant cue-related contrasts were modeled at cue onset (reward levels vs control), and group-level voxelwise results are reported: a whole-brain analysis (FWE-corrected) for main effects and a small-volume-corrected ROI analysis (FWE) in the nucleus accumbens showing an interaction. Key methodological details (participant age/sex counts, cue types, MRI field strength = 1.5T, preprocessing/statistics using SPM5) are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie (and low-calorie) food > neutral/baseline, reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results with cluster-familywise correction and tables of MNI coordinates, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T Siemens Verio), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT). Although the paper also reports seed-based connectivity and resting-state analyses, it clearly includes qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (food vs. non-food images). It includes within-participant contrasts (food > non-food) at the group level, reporting voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-level FWE-corrected) with tables of local maxima and figures. Methods report participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (food pictures), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The study therefore satisfies all inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-subject contrasts, and is empirical). Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete.

This study does not meet the key within-participant cue>control contrast requirement for reward-related cue-reactivity. While it is a high-resolution fMRI study using visual conditioned stimuli (fractals) that include monetary win cues (I3) and it reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (small-volume-corrected pallidal activation for shock CS value) (I5), as well as acceptable reporting of voxelwise results (I6) and participant/method details (I7), it does not present a qualifying within-subject contrast of natural reward (win) cues > control stimuli: win-related habenula responses were not significant and whole-brain/task-evoked win contrasts did not yield significant activations (high-vs-low win showed only a trend), and the only SVC-corrected win-related result reported pertains to a PPI connectivity analysis (connectivity, not task-evoked activation). Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (natural rewards), with clear within-participant contrasts (food vs. objects and high- vs low-palatable foods). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported with small-volume (ROI) cluster-size correction and peak coordinates (tables/figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Results and methods report participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of highly desirable > less desirable food images and all food > non-food images at the first level, and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain paired t-test with coordinates and p-values, as well as small-volume-corrected analyses for insula and putamen). Necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, 3-T MRI field strength, preprocessing with SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes the required within-subject cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity that includes clear visual cues (images of milkshake vs water) signaling impending milkshake delivery. It reports within-participant contrasts (milkshake cue > tasteless solution cue; milkshake receipt > tasteless solution receipt). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (cluster-corrected via Monte Carlo simulations) with coordinates in tables and figures; ROI analyses with voxel-wise FWE correction are also reported. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, DARTEL, AFNI modules) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-participant contrasts (HC vs LC and food vs non-food), and provides participant/sample and MRI details. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual food cues), I4 (within-participant cue contrasts), and I7 (age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing software reported). However, the reported group-level voxelwise results are confined to anatomically defined ROIs (VTA and hypothalamus) and assessed at an uncorrected voxelwise threshold (P<0.05) without reporting whole-brain results or small-volume-corrected (SVC) statistics. Therefore it fails I5. This meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain or SVC-corrected voxelwise result). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Accordingly, exclude.

This fMRI study tests neural responses to social (natural) vs monetary rewards using visual cues (dynamic video clips). It includes within-participant contrasts of reward cues > control cues (e.g., social reward vs social control; monetary reward vs monetary control) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (main effects and contrasts) plus a small-volume-corrected ROI result in the nucleus accumbens (FWE-corrected). Coordinates and statistical maps/tables are reported. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing/analysis) are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (positive social IAPS images) with within-participant contrast positive>neutral. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (cluster-corrected maps reported; Figure 4) and extracts ROI estimates; preprocessing and analysis software and MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio; Nipype/FSL/FreeSurfer/ANTs) and participant demographics are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and the preferred reporting elements in I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cues (food and physical-activity images) probing cue-reactivity/inhibitory responses. The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing reward-related cues vs control stimuli (food > non-food; active > inactive) and provides group-level voxelwise results obtained with SPM8, thresholded at P < 0.05 FWE (cluster-level) with reported coordinates. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistics are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for natural reward visual cue-reactivity and provides qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results.

The study uses visual food stimuli and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results, but it investigates neural responses to disgusting (aversive) food scenes contrasted against appetizing food baseline. Inclusion: I3 (visual natural food cues), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I6 (results clearly available in figures/tables), and I7 (participant age/sex and methods reported) are satisfied. However, it does NOT provide a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., appetizing>control) required by I4; instead the primary contrasts assess disgusting>appetizing and intensity of disgust (high vs moderate). Therefore it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of reward-related cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts (highly desirable > less desirable food cues; food > non-food) and uses group-level voxelwise analyses with small-volume correction (SVC) reporting FWE-corrected peak results (Supplementary Table S2, Figures). Imaging parameters (3T scanner, TR/TE) and participant information are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and (partially) I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. The study conducted within-participant food-vs-control contrasts from an event-related visual food-cue reactivity task and performed a random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analysis (corrected, using AFNI AlphaSim). Results are reported in figures and a supplementary table (Fig. 1, Table S1). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain result), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts (highly desirable > less desirable food; all food > nonfood) and uses group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with FWE correction; results are reported as cluster/peak coordinates and figures. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistics software (SPM8), and participant age/sex. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content is complete.

This study examined neural responses to appetizing food images (natural rewards) using visual stimuli and a passive viewing localizer. It includes a within-participant contrast of Food > Places & Clocks, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (TFCE-corrected) with coordinates and supplementary tables/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, TFCE) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, and is empirical fMRI data). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical BOLD-fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food pictures. It includes within-participant contrasts of food cues > control (directional arrow) events, reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (FWE-corrected p<0.05) with cluster tables/figures, and describes preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, FSL) and participant demographics (women, age range). Core methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text (supporting methods referenced for MRI parameters). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or resting-state, and include qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study includes within-participant contrasts of food vs. nonfood images and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain FWE correction (P < 0.001) in figures and text. Participant demographics and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, AFNI) are reported. MRI field strength was not stated, but that alone does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses visual food stimuli (natural rewards) and reports group-level voxelwise/small-volume-corrected results, but it does not include a within-participant contrast of reward-cues > control stimuli (i.e., a standard cue-reactivity contrast). The reported contrasts focus on choice/self-control (Challenge > No Challenge), value representations, and parametric modulators of taste/health during decisions rather than passive cue>control comparisons. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for a within-participant cue-reactivity contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward stimuli), I5 (group-level voxelwise/SVC results reported), I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures), I7 (participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (milkshake vs water images). It includes within-participant contrasts of milkshake cue > tasteless-solution cue and milkshake receipt > tasteless receipt, and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses corrected for multiple comparisons with coordinates and cluster sizes. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12; AFNI for cluster correction) and many methodological details are provided in the full text. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue-reactivity and voxelwise task-evoked results.

This study reports an fMRI task in which visual cues signaled potential monetary rewards (blank card, shuffling hands, and up/down arrows), constituting natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity. It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts of reward anticipation>baseline and outcome>baseline. The paper reports group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain analyses and corrected clusters (MNI coordinates and corrected p-values are provided; supplementary tables referenced), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind crossover fMRI study used visual food cues (highly desirable, less desirable) and non-food controls and reports within-participant contrasts (food > non-food; highly > less desirable). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are presented with a family-wise-error (FWE)–corrected peak in the right orbitofrontal cortex (coordinates reported). MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) and participant age/sex are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies and do not trigger any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food commercials). It includes a within-participant contrast of food>nonfood commercials (task-evoked food vs control) used in analyses. The paper reports group-level voxelwise (whole-brain, cluster-corrected) results: a between-subjects voxelwise contrast (AT+AA vs TT) for the food>nonfood maps, with cluster-corrected significance and MNI coordinates reported. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, FreeSurfer) are provided. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrast, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

E3: The study reports fMRI results using an a priori ventral striatal ROI (averaged z-statistic across the mask) as the primary outcome and summarizes mean/maximum activation in that ROI. The full text does not present qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables that would meet I5. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI reward-related paradigm with clear visual cues in the Monetary Incentive Delay task), I4 (within-participant contrast: reward-anticipation > neutral), and I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked result reported). Therefore excluded under E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual reward-related cue-reactivity: participants viewed visual object cues associated with monetary reward, loss, or neutral outcomes while undergoing fMRI. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing reward- vs neutral- and loss- vs neutral-associated cues, reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses including whole-brain searchlight and cluster-thresholded maps, and provides participant age/sex, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CoSMo-MVPA). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.
